key_insight: Single-qubit re-uploading circuits can match the expressivity of wider multi-qubit circuits for 1D inputs, but they train less reliably because their parameters are phase-locked and provide too few independent first-order directions.
engineering_relevance: For quantum machine learning, this means depth-for-width compression may preserve function class while increasing optimization difficulty, so circuit design must consider trainability, not just expressivity.
method: Analyzed angle-encoded variational circuits as truncated Fourier series under a fixed encoding budget E.
Proved the serial single-qubit circuit has at most 2E+2 tangent directions despite spanning the same 2E+1 Fourier coefficients.
Compared training success of serial circuits versus a two-qubit control on synthetic flat-spectrum targets and real time-series data using gradient descent, Adam, and Levenberg–Marquardt.
evidence_signal: Across experiments, the serial circuit consistently converged less often than the two-qubit control: at E=32 it succeeded only 3/100, 53/100, and 83/100 times under gradient descent, Adam, and Levenberg–Marquardt, while the control reached 99–100/100; similar gaps appeared on three real-world series.
watch_item: The advantage of the wider control is empirical and optimization-dependent, so results may vary with initialization, optimizer choice, and dataset spectrum.
paper_title: Same Spectrum, Harder First-Order Training: Phase-Locking in Single- versus Multi-Qubit Re-Uploading Circuits
